contrasts.line: Strive means pushing with all your effort for a prize; toil means long, tiring labour.
Strive aims all your effort at winning or reaching something; tinker means small repair changes.
Strive is all-out effort toward a target; persevere means not quitting after trouble.
Toil is long, tiring labour; strive is effort aimed at reaching a prize or result.
Toil means heavy, tiring labour; tinker means small changes to make something work.
Toil focuses on exhausting labour; persevere focuses on not quitting after setbacks.
Tinker means making small repair changes; strive means pushing strongly toward a result.
Tinker is little repair adjustments; toil is long, tiring labour.
Tinker changes parts bit by bit; persevere means carrying on after problems.
Persevere means not quitting after trouble; strive means using all effort for a result.
Persevere is staying with it after setbacks; toil is long, tiring labour.
Persevere means not quitting; tinker means making small repair changes.
Striving is straining hard toward a goal; improvising is making do on the spot with what is there.
Toiling is long exhausting work; improvising is a quick clever fix without preparation.
Tinkering fiddles and adjusts over time; improvising invents in the moment when plans fall through.
Persevering keeps going at the same task; improvising switches to whatever is at hand.
Improvising is unprepared and in the moment; striving is a determined push toward a goal.
Improvising is quick and unplanned; toiling is heavy work that goes on and on.
Improvising happens when there is no plan; tinkering is patient fiddling to make something work.
Improvising is a burst of quick invention; persevering is refusing to quit over the long haul.

Fairness pass by claude 2026-11-12: toil s13 is now historical mill labour (no setback to overcome); persevere s26/s28 now hinge on repeated failure then success, so neither is plain hard labour.
